MetaTrader4.item17: Market Order: A market order is an instruction to buy or sell financial instruments at the current market price. It will immediately execute at the best available price in the market.
MetaTrader4.item18: Listing: Listing is an order to buy or sell a financial instrument at a specific price in the future, and once the price is reached, it will be executed. MT4 offers four types of listings:
MetaTrader4.item19: Buy Stop: Located above the current market price, used to buy at a higher price when the market moves in the expected direction.
MetaTrader4.item20: Sell Stop: Located below the current market price, used to sell at a lower price when the market moves in the expected direction.
MetaTrader4.item21: Buy Limit: Located below the current market price, used to buy at a lower price when the market withdraws and reaches a specified level.
MetaTrader4.item22: Sell Limit: Located above the current market price, used to sell at a higher price when the market withdraws and reaches a specific level.
MetaTrader4.item23: Stop loss order: A stop loss order is used to limit the potential loss of an open position. It is set at a specific price worse than the current market price, suitable for long positions, and set at a better price than the current market price for short positions. If the market reaches this price, the stop loss order will become a market price order, closing the position.
MetaTrader4.item24: Profit order: A profit order is used to lock in the profit of an open position. It is set at a specific price that is better than the current market price, suitable for long positions, and set at a price worse than the current market price for short positions. When the market reaches this price, the profit order will become a market price order, closing the position.

advantagesCfds.item4: CFD stands for ‘Contract for Difference’ and is a contract between two parties agreeing to exchange the difference in the value of a security, instrument, or other asset between the time at which the CFD is opened and the time at which it is closed.
advantagesCfds.item5: CFDs are extremely versatile products growing in popularity as a short term investment tool. They provide an efficient way of maximizing your capital outlay and can help diversify your existing investment portfolio or hedge a position. Some of the advantages of trading CFDs are listed below.
advantagesCfds.item6: Speculate in Both Rising and Falling Markets
advantagesCfds.item7: CFDs are derivatives based on an underlying instrument. There is no ownership of the underlying asset, however they allow you to participate in the price movement of the asset. This means you can potentially profit in both rising and falling markets.
advantagesCfds.item8: In a rising market you would look to buy a CFD and then sell at a later date. This is called ‘going long’.
advantagesCfds.item9: In a falling market you would look to sell a CFD position first and then buy it back at a later date closing out the position. This is known as ‘going short’.
advantagesCfds.item11: CFDs are leveraged products enabling traders to increase their exposure to an underlying asset with a small initial outlay. When you open a trade you only need to deposit a small percentage of the value of the position and this is known as margin. Your margin will vary depending on the value of your CFD position. Leverage can result in added gains should the market move in your favour, however it also carries risks and can result in increased looses should your position move against you.
advantagesCfds.item13: The ability ‘go long’ as well as ‘go short’ with CFDs means that they are a great tool for hedging an existing portfolio. They are a cost effective alternative to selling the portfolio prematurely and can be used to provide ‘insurance’ against adverse price movements.
advantagesCfds.item14: For example, if you have a long-term portfolio that you wish to keep, however you are of the view that there is some short term risk to the value of the portfolio you could use CFDs to ‘hedge’ your positions. If the value of the portfolio falls the profit you make on the CFDs will offset the losses in your portfolio.
advantagesCfds.item16: The contract sizes of CFDs are often less than the typical contract size of the underlying instrument which means you can gain exposure to the price movement of the instrument without a significant deposit. Flexible sizing allows you to tailor your trading according to your risk management criteria.
advantagesCfds.item18: CFDs allow traders access to a wide range of global markets that would otherwise be difficult to access. CFDs make it easy to trade CFDs on Commodities like Gold, Silver, Oil, as well as a variety of global indices without having to trade the futures contract itself.
advantagesCfds.item20: You should always consider your risk appetite and investment strategy prior to trading leveraged products. Leverage can work for you as well as against you and can magnify profits as well as losses. In the event of a significant move against you, you may lose more than your initial deposit. advantagesForex.item11: Trade Both Rising and Falling Markets
advantagesForex.item12: There are no restrictions in the Forex market as to which direction you can trade. Similarly, if you believe the pair is going to decrease in value you could sell it, or ‘go short’.
advantagesForex.item14: The amount required to trade Forex is generally lower than what would be required to trade other financial markets. In addition to this, multiple desktop and mobile trading platforms make it easy to access the Forex markets at any time.
